convergence.comparison: pixelmatch threshold 0.1, per-state budget 1.0% (dispatch default; contract pixelThreshold 0.03 is the Gate-1 story budget); targets = NORMALIZED prototype, contract root #cs-ov-types, Chromium (playwright 1.58 / Chromium 151 headless shell), viewports 1280x1400 (default) / 480x1400 (narrow-single-column) per states.json story.viewport, deviceScaleFactor 2, --disable-lcd-text --font-render-hinting=none (GC-009 capture fact: grayscale-unhinted matches pen's rasterizer), fonts ready + double-rAF quiescence, animations/transitions frozen. ALIGNMENT (v002 signature): the default state's root y-offset is fractional (341.5 CSS px, per the states.json capture note — re-verified this run) and screenshot rasterization rounds it by one device row unpredictably; the target renderer clips 2 CSS px tall of the element box, locates the tile-0 top-border row by the v002 signature (two consecutive device rows ≈ #D5D3D0 at three straight-segment sample columns clear of the 24-device-px corner arcs — the v001 signature keyed on the retired gradient's catline-from blue and no longer applies), and crops the exact 2048x608 / 880x1272 content band from it.
convergence.iterationNotes: Iteration 1 converged both states at ~0.003% (32 isolated single-pixel glyph-AA residuals per state — the same residual level v001 recorded — sub-threshold everywhere else). One uncounted infra correction to the compare harness's TARGET renderer, not the .pen: the initial fractional-CSS-px clip landed the content band one device row low (full-width false diff at every edge, 1.55% on default); replaced with the deterministic top-border-signature alignment above (same class as v001's uncounted crop correction). The .pen itself needed zero fix rounds: geometry was carried from the v001 approved document (states.json v002 $comment: extract-verify box identical, tiles 138px, the restyle is color/mechanism-only) with the outline rebound from the retired gradient to the created solid role token.
convergence.geometryProbesDetail: Probes derived from design-rules 1-6 and the states.json G-vectors, asserted on the exports (26 per state, 52/52 pass): frame dims 2048x608 / 880x1272 (G1 grid 1024x304, G2 grid 440x636 at scale 2); tile origins (0,0)/(1052,0)/(0,332)/(1052,332) device px at default and (0,0)/(0,332)/(0,664)/(0,996) at narrow via border sampling; THE v002 MECHANISM PROBES — per tile, top border row ≈ #D5D3D0 AND bottom border row ≈ #D5D3D0 (uniform: the identity of top and bottom border color is the pixel-level assertion that the v001 dark-on-top gradient is gone, design-rules 3), left/right straight-edge border columns ≈ #D5D3D0 at mid-height (sampled clear of the 12px corner arcs); tile interiors white surface; 28px gaps white (backdrop shows through — no second border, no shadow, design-rules 3/6).

tokenJudgmentCalls.prototypeValue: light #D5D3D0 (--border-strong, 'no blue anywhere'); dark #A5BCFC (--seq6 dark ramp, 'light blue only') — DIFFERENT source tokens per mode (flags.json V2-P1 mapping wrinkle)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: No existing Hemlock border role carries the (light gray, dark light-blue) pair — verified against the LIVE hemlock-library.lib.pen, not just the skill copy: sem-borders-muted matches light exactly ($prim-gray-200 #D5D3D0) but goes navy in dark ($prim-navy-200 #2A3A5C), directly contradicting Bill's explicit dark intent; sem-borders-action-subtle has the dark value as its LIGHT value. Deliberately NOT bound to sem-borders-muted (would silently discard the contracted-in-rules dark intent) and NOT hue-matched per mode across two roles (a T2 bind is one role carrying its own pair). Created the single semantic role per the never-stop gap doctrine; this RETIRES the four v001 provisional gradient tokens (sem-borders-categoryOutline-from/-to/-mix70/-mix35) and re-points the open designer-review item, exactly as flags.json V2-P1 and design-rules 14 direct.

tokenJudgmentCalls.surface: caps category label text (h4, all tiles, both states)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: Carried from v001 (DJ-001) and re-verified at v002: the label KEEPS its blue (design-rules 7 — the 'no blue' clause governs the outline only). The label is NON-interactive brand-accent text; Hemlock has no dedicated eyebrow/label text role, and sem-text-action owns accent-colored text. Value-identity in BOTH modes (light #3A6AF8; dark #5A82F9 = the template's dark --accent exactly); flagged because 'action' implies interactivity the tiles do not have (design-rules 10).

tokenJudgmentCalls.surface: backdrop behind the grid gaps (frame fill)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: Carried from v001 (DJ-002) and re-verified at v002: the contract root has no background of its own; the 28px gaps show the white page/card. In the GenUI serving context the component sits on mainPanel's surface (sem-background-surface, white light / navy-700 dark — and the template's dark --page-bg is #131C31 = navy-700 exactly, identity in both modes). Not sem-background-main (taupe).

tokenJudgmentCalls.surface: body copy (p, all tiles, both states)
tokenJudgmentCalls.rationale: Light is identity ($prim-gray-700 #403D3A). Recorded rather than silent because the DARK values diverge: the template's dark body (#C9D4EA) is not Hemlock's sem-text-body dark ($prim-navylight-600 #B3C1DB). Dark is uncontracted (states.json themes: light only; design-rules 13) and the bind is by ROLE — the body-copy role is unambiguous, so the Hemlock dark value governs when dark arrives. The divergence is template-wide (Bill's dark ramp), not component-specific; no token created.
